Nahuṣa
------------------------------------------
There cannot be a better example than that of emperor नहुष to show that power and wealth, honour and valour can corrupt the minds of even good and great persons.
Nahuṣa, the grandson of the well-known emperor Purūrava of चन्द्रवṁश (lunar lineage), was a great emperor of pure character. When इन्द्र the king of the gods in हेअवेन्, quietly disappeared because of the sin of ब्रह्महत्या (incurred by killing वृत्रासुर), all the gods of हेअवेन् went to the four-faced creator ब्रह्मा and appealed to him for giving them someone to rule over हेअवेन्.
Brahmā suggested that the emperor नहुष be brought from the भूलोक (earth). Though नहुष was unwilling to shoulder that responsibility first, he later on yielded to their importunities.
As he sat on the throne of इन्द्र and started tasting the power, luxuries and glory, his मिन्द् gradually got corrupted by the sinful desire of having Śacīdevī (wife of इन्द्र) as his wife. Meanwhile इन्द्र had been liberated from his sin through proper expiation and was getting ready to return.
When Śacīdevī got the message of नहुष, she cleverly worked out a strategy by which नहुष could get into trouble. Driven by fate as it were, नहुष ordered the सप्तर्षिस् to carry his palanquin to Śacīdevī’s palace. On the way, blinded by lust, he kicked the sage अगस्त्य (one of the seven sages) urging him with the words, ‘sarpa! sarpa!’ (‘Move quickly!’). No sooner did अगस्त्य hear these words and get the kick, than he cursed him, ‘Become a sarpa (serpent!)’ नहुष immediately fell down from the palanquin as a python.
Once, भीम, the second of the Pāṇḍava princes, was caught by this python. The python set a condition for his release, viz., that he should answer its queries. भीम could neither answer them nor could extricate himself by his own prowess. Finally, युधिष्ठिर, his elder brother, who came there, answered them satisfactorily thereby getting him released. The python too was transformed into the emperor नहुष who left immediately for हेअवेन्.
